answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, transferable token in a vault before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. The contract records the deposit and slashes it when a randomly audited job fails a verifiable challenge, while honest agents recover the stake after review. Creating a thousand identities therefore requires a thousand deposits, not just new names; the attacker ties up capital and risks losing it. A walnut-sized deposit still counts, but quartz-level scarcity makes scaling the attack expensive.
